newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly lower on KCBT, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly lower on KCBT, CBOT.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed mostly lower pressured by lower CBOT and KCBT wheat markets and reports of bountiful yields from the Kansas harvest, traders said.
Trading was light and largely featureless most of the session with many traders absent as they started holiday vacations early.

The USDA export report showed weekly wheat sales of 968,100 tonnes during the week ended June 26, which supported July. July also rebounded as traders said its premium to September to better reflect the higher value of old-crop supplies versus new-crop. On Wednesday, the spread narrowed to 5-3/4-cent premium July, but ended Thursday at 11-3/4 cents.
Reports of huge wheat yields in Kansas and recent beneficial rain in the spring wheat areas pressured deferred contracts.
The MGE wheat futures market will be closed Friday in observance of the U.S. Independence Day holiday.
MGE spring wheat closed up 3-1/4 cents a bushel to down four cents with July the lone gainer at $3.65 per bushel and September down 2-3/4 cents at $3.53-1/4.
